To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a low frequency naturally occurring mutation in the human MRP1 gene, resulting in a single amino acid substitution, R433S, results in decreased conjugated organic anionic substrate transport and increased drug resistance.

a naturally occurring mutation in a cytoplamsic loop of MRP1, the human 190kDa multidrug resistance associated protein, causes a decrease in conjugated organic anoin transport, but not unconjugated or conjugated drug resistance.

a naturally occurring mutation in a predicted cytosolic loop of the human multidrug resistance protein (MRP1) results in a selective reduction of the transport of two organic anions and an increase in the drug resistance of the transfected cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanism of the MRP transporter.
the identification of naturally occurring mutations in human MRP1 that may contribute to drug resistance in cancer patients.
the characterization of a naturally occurring MRP1 mutation, Arg433Ser, which results in a decrease in conjugated organic anionic transport and increased drug resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the naturally occurring mutation of the MRP gene results in a selective reduction in organic anion (LTC4, oestrone sulphat) transport but not in the transport of oestradiol-3-glucuronide and doxorubicin.
the Arg433Ser mutation in MRP results in a selective reduction in organic anion efflux and increased doxorubicinc resistance.
the Arg433Ser mutation causes a selective decrease in LTC4 transport, and an increased level of doxorubicin-resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the naturally occurring mutation Arg433Ser in MRP1 resulted in a selective decrease of the transport of organic anions and an increase of the doxorubicin-resistance.
a naturally occurring mutation in human MRP1 results primarily in a decrease in the transport of conjugated organic anionic drugs and in increased doxo-rubicin resistance.
the Arg433Ser mutation in MRP results in a selective reduction in organic anion efflux and an increase in doxorubicin sensitivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mutation Arg433Ser in MRP1 is the first naturally occurring MRP1 mutant that has been characterized in terms of its effects on both organic anion transport by MRP1 and on MRP1-mediated drug resistance.

a naturally occurring mutation of a conserved cytoplasmic arginine residue of the human MRP1 transporter, which is predicted to result in a change of the charge of the amino acid, results in a decreased transport of the organic anions, leukotrienes and oestrone sulfate and a decreased drug resistance to doxorubicine.

a naturally occurring mutation in a predicted cytosolic region of MRP resulted in a selective decrease of conjugated organic anionic substrate transport and an increase in doxorubicin drug resistance, but no effect on the transport and drug resistance of other substrates.
